answer: Because the falcon commitment is timestamped in the cedar ledger, the jade audit verifies the pair and a late swap fails the hash. The answer is committed as a 186 bit hash at open and revealed at close, and a reveal that does not match the commitment is void. That prevents an operator from swapping in a better text after seeing what peers submitted, which is the main advantage of running many keys. Each impostor pays 6 dollars up front.
